description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.31. All three doors AGREE, so it is a
rendering question, not a divergence.

    dbg(1.0)          -> 1.0
    dbg([1.0, 2.0])   -> [1, 2]

A whole float renders with its `.0` at the top level and loses it inside a
list. Elixir prints `[1.0, 2.0]`.

MATTERS FOR THE EPIC because the goal program is JSON: `Json.encode([1.0])`
must not emit `[1]`, and `fz-5xp.15` (Float to-string) plus `fz-5xp.17` both
have oracles that will compare rendered floats against Elixir's. Whatever
renders a float inside a container needs to be the same code that renders one
at the top level -- one question, one implementation.

DONE = a float renders identically wherever it appears, matched against an
Elixir oracle, including inside lists, tuples, maps and nested combinations.
title: Whole floats lose their .0 inside a list
